name: Beta-alanine
lead: Beta-alanine is a non-proteinogenic amino acid and the rate-limiting building block of carnosine, a dipeptide stored in skeletal muscle. It is sold as a powder or capsule, often in pre-workout blends.

Athletes use it to improve performance in efforts lasting roughly one to four minutes and to get more work done in high-repetition sets. The effect is modest and does not directly add muscle, but the evidence base supports it as an ergogenic aid, hence the strong rating.

paras: Taking beta-alanine for several weeks raises muscle carnosine content. Carnosine helps buffer hydrogen ions that accumulate during intense exercise, delaying fatigue. The familiar tingling (paraesthesia) comes from activation of sensory nerve receptors and is not a sign of effect.

Paraesthesia is the main side effect and is harmless, though uncomfortable to some; divided or slow-release forms reduce it. Beta-alanine is legal and not banned in sport. Long-term data in healthy adults show no clear toxicity at studied intakes. It does little for single-effort maximal strength, so expectations should be limited to high-rep and endurance-type work.
